s: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

s: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

s: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

s: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

s: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

s: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

s: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

s: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.
quote: Zone 1 - Business Districts outside of Manhattan (e.g., Downtown Brooklyn, Downtown Flushing, and Jamaica; Manhattan 125th Street) $2.50 $5.00 Zone 2 - Neighborhood Retail Districts $2.00 $3.00 Zone 3 - All Other Metered Locations $1.50 $2.50

s: No resident street-parking permit programme is described on NYC DOT's Motorists & Parking, Parking Regulations, Parking Meters or Municipal Parking pages; the only permits listed there are for disability, clergy, agency business and highway travel.
No guest or visitor street-parking permit is described on the NYC DOT pages read (Motorists & Parking, Parking Regulations).

NYC DOT garages sell monthly permits: Court Square (Queens) $400, Borough Hall (Brooklyn) $330, Bay Ridge $275, Jerome-190th Street (Bronx) $250, Delancey and Essex (Manhattan) $600. No monthly rate is listed for the Queens Family Court garage in Jamaica.
Monthly garage permits are reserved online, first come first served, from five days before the month starts; a New York State driver's licence check is run at reservation.
quote: Reservations open on the website five days before the first of the month at 10 am. All reservations are made for the upcoming month, on a first-come, first-served basis. A New York State Department of Motor Vehicles driver's license check is performed at the time of the reservation.

s: Municipal parking fields (open lots) do not allow overnight parking; they close at the posted hour, typically 10 PM.
quote: Municipal parking fields do not allow overnight parking. The fields close as shown in the posted regulations for each facility. Parking after posted hours may result in a summons and leaves the vehicle at risk as there is no security at the closed facilities.

s: Queens Family Court Municipal Parking Garage, 150-07 Archer Avenue by Jamaica station: open Mon-Sat 7 AM-9 PM, Sun 8 AM-8 PM; $5 first hour, $20 daily maximum.
quote: Queens Family Court Municipal Parking Garage - With EV Charging Spaces 150-07 Archer Avenue, Queens, NY 11435 (near Jamaica subway and LIRR station) 213 spaces (including 5 ADA accessible spaces & 3 Electric Vehicle charging spaces) Monday to Saturday, 7 AM to 9 PM Sunday: 8 AM to 8 PM

s: Quarterly permits at municipal parking fields: Flushing #4 $300, Steinway #1 (Astoria) $500, Bayside $500, Brighton Beach $625, Sheepshead Bay #1 $300, Canarsie $300, Bronxdale $400.
quote: Bronxdale Municipal Parking Field $400 Bensonhurst #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Brighton Beach Municipal Parking Field $625 Canarsie Municipal Parking Field $300 Sheepshead Bay #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Bayside Municipal Parking Field $500 Flushing #4 Municipal Parking Field $300 Steinway #1 Municipal Parking Field $500

s: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A licence costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.
quote: All dogs in New York City must have licenses, and the licenses must be attached to their collars while in public.

s: Licence fee: $8.50 a year if spayed or neutered; if not, $8.50 under 4 months old and $34 over 4 months.
quote: Licenses for spayed or neutered dogs of any age cost $8.50 per year. If your dog is not spayed or neutered, a license will cost $8.50 if the dog is under 4 months old, or $34 if it is older than 4 months.

s: In any public place a dog must be on a leash no longer than six feet.
quote: a person who owns, possesses or controls a dog shall not permit it to be in any public place or in any open or unfenced area abutting on a public place unless the dog is effectively restrained by a leash or other restraint not more than six feet long.

s: In city parks dogs must be leashed except where Parks rules allow off-leash; the Health Code lets Parks allow off-leash in unenclosed areas only within a window that starts no earlier than 9 PM and ends by 9 AM. The Parks rules themselves could not be read (site bot-walled).
quote: Such rules shall include provisions that prohibit unrestrained dogs in unenclosed DOPR controlled areas and facilities except during a specified range of time, that shall not begin earlier than 9:00 P.M. and not extend past 9:00 A.M.

s: With proof of a current licence and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash in NYC Parks dog runs. The open-data list has 95 active runs (14 in Queens, 20 Brooklyn, 41 Manhattan, 15 Bronx, 5 Staten Island); see dog_parks.csv.
quote: With proof of current dog license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash at New York City park dog runs

s: Owners must pick up after their dog in all public areas; the fine is up to $250.
quote: If you do not clean up after your dog, you may be fined up to $250.

s: No limit on the number of dogs per household was found in Health Code Article 161 section headings or on the NYC Health dog licence page.
Beach and boardwalk dog rules (seasonal bans) could not be collected: nycgovparks.org returned a 403 bot wall on the first request and was not retried.
From December 1 to March 31, no parking on any village road whenever 2 or more inches of snow falls, until 24 hours after the snow stops or plowing is finished; fine up to $100.
quote: There is no parking on any village roadways between December 1st through March 31st whenever 2 or more inches of snow falls, until 24 hours after the snow has stopped falling or when plowing has been fully completed, whichever comes first. Vehicle owners may face a fine of up to $100.

s: The village lists municipal lots to move a car to under the snow ordinance; the Harrison Avenue garage still charges during snow.
quote: Harrison Garage 200 First Street (MUST PAY TO PARK, EVEN DURING SNOW)

s: Commuter parking permits are for village residents only; the driver licence and vehicle registration must both show the Mineola address and plate on the application, so an out-of-state registration would not match.
quote: Commuter Parking Permits are available to village residents only. A copy of a valid driver license and vehicle registration must be provided and match the license plate and Mineola address listed on the application.

s: Special Parking Permits are only for owners and employees of businesses in the village, not for residents.
quote: Special Parking Permits will only be issued to owners and/or employees of businesses located within the Incorporated Village of Mineola and are only valid while the permit holder is an employee of said business.

s: Harrison Avenue Parking Garage (200 First Street) monthly permits: overnight (24-hour) $120 for Mineola residents and $250 for non-residents; day (14-hour) $60 resident, $125 non-resident. Proof of residency required for the resident rate.
quote: Overnight Permit (24 Hour)/Mineola Resident * $120/month

s: Non-resident overnight (24-hour) monthly permit at the Harrison Avenue garage is $250.
quote: Overnight Permit (24 Hour)/Non-Resident $250/month

s: Town of Hempstead dog licence: $10 for a spayed or neutered dog (with vet certificate), $18 otherwise; proof of rabies vaccination needed. (Whether the Village of Hempstead licenses separately was not confirmed.)
quote: The fee for unneutered male and unspayed female dogs is $18 ($15 plus a $3 New York State mandated spay/neuter fee).

s: Overnight street parking is banned village-wide from 2 AM to 6 AM, every day of the year. Temporary overnight permission can be requested from the Police Department.
quote: Overnight on-street parking is prohibited between 2AM and 6AM. This regulation is Village-wide, 365 days per year, as posted on all roads leading into the Village. By request, temporary overnight on-street parking may be permitted.

s: For a guest or a one-off night, call the Police Department at (914) 834-1000 to ask for temporary overnight street parking.
quote: By request, temporary overnight on-street parking may be permitted. Please contact the Police Department at (914) 834-1000 for instructions.

s: Overnight parking is by permit in the village's nine municipal lots; annual and semi-annual permits are sold to residents, commuters and business owners through an online portal. Prices and vehicle-registration rules were not on the pages read.
quote: Generally, parking permits are required to park overnight, by day, or 24/7; however, regulations in individual lots may vary (check signage on-location). Temporary parking permits are also available for sale for short-term parking needs (up to two weeks).

s: Nine municipal lots; permits are annual or semi-annual (no monthly price found on the page).
quote: The Village offers annual and semi-annual parking permits for residents, commuters, and business owners/employees. A small selection of non-resident commuter permits are also available.

s: Dog licences for Larchmont residents are issued by the Town of Mamaroneck Clerk's Office. Fee not on the page read.
quote: The Town of Mamaroneck's Clerk's Office issues dog licenses and marriage licenses

s: Flint Park, the village's largest park, does not allow dogs.
quote: No Dogs Allowed (with exception of service animals) Flint Park is located at the end of Locust Avenue.

s: Manor Park (privately owned by the Larchmont Manor Park Society) is the only park that still allows leashed dog walks.
quote: It is the only park that still allows individuals to bring their dogs for a walk (on leashes).

s: Overnight street parking is banned citywide from 2 AM to 6 AM. Garage and lot permits are the alternative.
quote: Is overnight, on-street parking allowed in White Plains? No. The City has a long-standing ordinance which prohibits parking on the street between the hours of 2:00 AM - 6:00 AM.

s: Garage and lot permits are sold monthly, quarterly or annually. Resident-only permits need a lease or utility bill, a New York licence with a White Plains address and a vehicle registration with the same information, so an out-of-state licence or registration would not qualify for resident-only locations.
quote: Valid New York drivers license showing resident parker's name and a City of White Plains address Vehicle Registration for each plate number listed on permit with same information as license

s: The city runs eight garages and 23 surface lots; permits are sold monthly, quarterly or annually and guarantee a space. Monthly prices are on a separate garages-and-lots page that was not read.
quote: Customers may purchase most permits on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis (some restrictions apply) at a considerable discount from the published meter rates.

s: A $75 annual Resident Evening & Weekend Permit lets residents use most downtown garages Mon-Fri 6 PM-midnight and weekends 10 AM-midnight. No guest street permit was found.
quote: This permit is valid January through December at a cost of $75 and offers White Plains Residents the ability to utilize most downtown parking structures while dining or shopping.

s: Downtown street meters run Monday to Saturday 9 AM-9 PM (9 AM-6 PM outside downtown); street parking is free on Sundays and six holidays. Meters in lots and garages charge at all times.
quote: On-street meters require payment Monday through Saturday, in the downtown area from 9AM-9PM. On-street meters outside the downtown area require payment 9AM-6PM. On-street parking is free on Sundays

s: Do not park on the street when it snows or snow is forecast; cars left out may be plowed in and ticketed.
quote: DO NOT PARK CARS ON THE STREET WHEN IT SNOWS - OR WHEN SNOW IS IN THE FORECAST.

s: Every dog must be licensed. Fee: $10 for one year if spayed or neutered, $18 if not (two-year: $17 / $27).
quote: Spayed/Neutered $10.00 $17.00

s: Off the owner's property, dogs must be on a leash no longer than eight feet; fine up to $100.
quote: Section 2 - In all other cases, dog owners must have their dogs on leashes not exceeding eight feet in length. Violations are punishable by a fine of up to $100.

s: Owners must remove their dog's feces from any sidewalk, gutter, street or other public area.
quote: Section 3 - It shall be the duty of each dog owner to remove any feces left by his/her dog on any sidewalk, gutter, street or other public areas.

s: Two city dog parks, by permit: Bark Park (Main St. extension off Brockway Pl.) and Battle Hill Park. There is an area only for small or young dogs; a current licence tag is required. The Fall/Winter 2025-26 brochure lists the annual fee as $25 for up to 3 dogs per resident, $50 non-resident.
quote: Dogs with permits are welcome to run around and exercise at our Dog Park. This park features an area exclusively for small or young dogs.

s: The Town of Hempstead runs eight enclosed dog parks, each with separate small-dog and large-dog sections; the Newbridge Road park is open only to town residents.
quote: all parks have separate sections for small and large dogs.

s: Town roads are swept on a schedule from May to October (applies to unincorporated areas; village streets follow village rules).
quote: Beginning in May, town roadways are swept on a regular basis.

s: The Parking Bureau sells 24-hour permits for municipal lots (2,275 spaces): residents $100 a month ($1,110 a year), non-residents $175 a month. Proof of residence is required for the resident price.
quote: Resident 24-Hour Permit 24 Hour Permit Permit Fee Monthly $100 3 Month $300 6 Month $600 12 Month/Yearly December is FREE $1,110

s: Non-resident 24-hour lot permit: $175 a month, $2,100 a year.
quote: Non-Resident 24 Hour Permit 24 Hour Permit Permit Fee Monthly $175 3 Month $525

s: Permits are for municipal lots, bought in person at the Parking Bureau, 3 East Sidney Avenue, with proof of residence. Which documents count (lease, registration) is not stated on the page.
quote: Please note: Proof of residence must be shown when purchasing parking permits. Parking Permits may be obtained from the Mount Vernon Parking Bureau, located at 3 East Sidney Avenue, Mount Vernon.

s: When 3 or more inches of snow have fallen, cars on Snow Emergency Routes must be moved or risk a ticket and tow.
quote: When 3 or more inches of snow have fallen in the City of Mount Vernon, 'Snow Emergency Routes' become active and vehicles parked on the routes have to be moved, otherwise they risk being ticketed and then towed/impounded

s: From December 1 to April 15, alternate-side rules apply and overnight parking on a city street is not allowed unless a sign authorises it.
quote: A helpful "Parking Rule of Thumb" to use is that if there is no sign authorizing parking, then parking overnight on a city street is not permitted between December 1st and April 15th.

s: Alternate side-of-the-street parking is in effect from December 1 to April 15, as shown on street signs.
quote: Between December 1st and April 15th, alternate side-of-the-street parking rules are in effect. Parking regulations are indicated on street signs.

s: Meters are free on ten listed holidays (New Year's Day through Christmas Day). Meter hours were not on the page.
quote: Free Meter Parking On The Following Days New Year's Day Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr. Washington's Birthday (President's Day) Memorial Day Independence Day Labor Day Columbus Day Veterans Day Thanksgiving Day Christmas Day

s: Harrison has a resident parking sticker issued by the Police Department. Driver licence and registration must both come back to a Harrison address, and permits are not issued to out-of-town vehicles, so a car still registered in another state does not qualify until it is re-registered.
quote: Driver License and Registration MUST come back to a valid Harrison address. All warrants must be satisfied or permit will not be issued. Resident permits WILL NOT be issued to / for the following: Business Purposes, Commercial Vehicle, and Out of Town Vehicles.

s: How to apply: print the form and bring it to the Police Department, or scan and email it; questions 973-483-4101 option 1. Stickers are annual (2026 stickers valid to December 31, 2026). No fee is stated on the resident form.
quote: Print out the form, fill it out and bring it to the police Department.

s: The town also lists a Non-Resident Parking Permit application and a Special Circumstance Parking Permit; their terms were not read.
quote: Resident Parking Permit Application (PDF) Non-Resident Parking Permit Application (PDF) Commercial Parking Permit $300 (PDF) Commercial Parking Permit $500 (PDF) Special Circumstance Parking Permit (PDF)

s: Harrison Parking Center, 355 Somerset Street, is open 24/7. Monthly price was not on the page.
quote: Harrison Parking Center Address 355 Somerset Street, Harrison, NJ 07029 Parking Center Information (973) 350-7634 Hours of Operation Open 24/7

s: During snow, cars must be off the snow emergency routes: Harrison Avenue (Passaic Ave. to Schuyler Ave.) and Frank E. Rodgers Blvd. (Bergen Street to Scott Mobus Place); cars left there are ticketed and removed.
quote: During snow events, we ask all vehicles be removed from snow emergency routes. Harrison Avenue (Passaic Ave. to Schuyler Ave.) and Frank E. Rodgers Blvd. (North & South) (Bergen Street to Scott Mobus Place).

s: No parking while the road is snow covered on both sides of Angelo Cifelli Dr between Frank E Rodgers Blvd South and South 3rd St; violators are ticketed and towed.
quote: there will be No Parking while road is snow covered on both sides of Angelo Cifelli Dr, between Frank E Rodgers Blvd South and South 3rd St.

s: Dog licences are issued by the Harrison Clerk's Office, 318 Harrison Avenue (973-268-2425), not the Health Department. Fee not on the page.
quote: Please note the Harrison Board of Health Department no longer issues dog and cat licenses. To obtain a license, please contact the Harrison Clerk's Office at 973-268-2425 - located at 318 Harrison Avenue.

s: West New York enforces alternate-side (street sweeping) parking; cars must be moved during the posted sweeping hours. Enforcement pauses in winter and resumed March 16 in 2026.
quote: beginning Monday, March 16, 2026, the West New York Parking Services Utility will resume enforcement of alternate-side parking (street sweeping) regulations. Residents are kindly asked to move their vehicles during posted sweeping hours to avoid parking tickets.

s: The town has parking garages and municipal lots; prices rose June 1, 2024. The rate sheet itself was not read; Parking Services phone 201-295-1575.
quote: Effective June 1, 2024, the price of all parking facilities will increase.

s: Any vehicle parked on the street in North Bergen between 10 PM and 7 AM needs a permit. Visitors may park up to 3 hours without a permit between 7 AM and 10 PM.
quote: B. All visiting vehicles may park up to 3 hours without a permit between 7:00 am and 10:00 pm . Vehicles that will be parked longer than 3 hours will require a permit. C. Any vehicle parking within the Township from 10:00 pm to 7:00 am requires a permit

s: All resident vehicles need a Parking Authority permit to park in the township.
quote: A. All resident vehicles are required to have a permit to park within the Township.

s: New residents (including with a car not yet re-registered) can register online for a two-month new-resident permit: $20 per vehicle, valid 60 days, with a valid driver's licence, valid vehicle registration and a lease or deed.
quote: New Resident online registration is for new residents moving into North Bergen. This is a two-month registration, for a non-commercial vehicle, to provide you time to update your residency documentation as you transition to your new North Bergen residence.

s: New-resident permit fee: $20 per vehicle, valid 60 days from approval.
quote: Fee: $20.00 per vehicle; Valid 60 days from the date of Approval Confirmation

s: A visitor needs an overnight permit bought at a Parking Authority pay station ($10 at the machine, 24/7), showing the ID of the resident being visited.
quote: Visitors must visit our pay stations for an OVERNIGHT permit

s: The Parking Authority rents spaces in its lots to residents only, including resident overnight rentals 6 PM-9 AM. Prices were not on the page.
quote: Business Rentals: Mon-Fri 9AM - 6PM Resident Overnight Rental: 6PM - 9AM

s: Resident Permit Parking Program: decals cost $15 a year for the first vehicle, $25 second, $50 third, $100 fourth and above. Needs an NJ licence and NJ registration showing the West New York address, plus proof of residency; apply in person at 224 60th Street.
quote: The first vehicle in the household will be $15.00 for a one-year period; the second vehicle $25.00; the third vehicle $50.00; and the fourth vehicle and above will be $100.00 for each permit.

s: A car with out-of-state plates can get an Out-of-State Plate Permit with proof of residency: $50 for three months.
quote: Parking permits are issued to individuals upon presentation of proof of residency to use on their out-of-state registered vehicles. Out-of-state permits can be purchased at a cost of $50.00 for a period of three (3) months.

s: New residents get a free two-week Temporary Permit while they change the address on their licence and registration.
quote: we provide a two (2) week Temporary Permit free of charge so new residents have sufficient time to change the address on their driver's license and vehicle registration.

s: Visitor permits are issued for one vehicle and allow parking near the residence, except during posted street cleaning or emergency restrictions.
quote: Vehicles displaying this permit may park near the residence for which the permit is issued, except during posted street cleaning periods or temporary/emergency restrictions.

s: Residential permit holders do not pay for overnight parking in non-reserved municipal lots.
quote: Holders of valid residential permits need not pay for overnight parking at any non-reserve municipal parking lot.
